Start From Any Project

Four entry points, one tool. Every path ends the same way: a confirmed task queue, a forecasted cost, and agents behind test gates.

ANew project — empty folder, no code, no specs

forge init prepares the directory (stack detection, git, baseline checks). forge wizard scans it, asks a clarifying question or two if your request is ambiguous, and drafts the whole setup with a cost forecast. You confirm the draft — that's gate #1 — and run. With the default careful profile every task pauses for your forge accept.

$ forge init --target ./new-project
[init] stack: python · git initialized · baseline green
$ forge wizard --target ./new-project \
  --prompt "CLI calculator: package calc, python -m calc 2 3, pytest tests"
[wizard] 4 tasks drafted · forecast ≈ $0.20 → tasks.wizard.yaml
$ forge run --tasks ./new-project/tasks.wizard.yaml --target ./new-project
$ forge accept init-package && forge resume run-…
$ forge report --plain
[done] 4 of 4 tasks · $0.16 · 2 repairs

BLegacy project — lots of code, no spec, no AGENTS.md

The wizard reads the tree, finds the real test commands, and runs them as a baseline before any model call — a red baseline is an honest stop, not a surprise mid-run. Recipes (config/recipes/) draft a queue deterministically, with zero LLM cost: test-coverage is the safest first move on legacy code.

$ forge wizard --target ./legacy --recipe test-coverage
[recipe] module path? → src/auth · test command? → python -m pytest -q
[wizard] draft ready · no LLM call · $0
$ forge lint ./legacy/tasks.wizard.yaml
[lint] contract OK · acceptance passable at every DAG position
$ forge run --tasks ./legacy/tasks.wizard.yaml --target ./legacy

CDocumented project — AGENTS.md, SPEC.md, canon/ docs

What's already written gets used. AGENTS.md in the target root goes straight into the coder's context; forge import turns an existing SPEC.md into a task draft via the planner; --spec attaches a spec excerpt to every task prompt and canon_snapshot pins a canonical decisions file. canon/ is always read-only for agents.

$ forge import --spec ./project/SPEC.md --out tasks.draft.yaml
[planner] 6 tasks drafted from SPEC.md — review before launch (gate #1)
$ forge lint tasks.draft.yaml
$ forge run --tasks tasks.draft.yaml \
  --target ./project --spec ./project/SPEC.md

DHands-on — your own tasks.yaml, full control

Write the queue yourself: DAG dependencies, gitignore-like scopes, shell acceptance commands, per-task budgets, milestone gates. forge lint validates the contract before you spend anything, --dry-run prints the cost forecast, and the read-only UI gives you a kanban while the run is going.

$ forge lint tasks.yaml
$ forge run --tasks tasks.yaml --dry-run
[dry-run] 5 tasks · worst-case $1.40 · nothing executed
$ forge run --tasks tasks.yaml --target ./repo
$ forge ui # kanban on http://127.0.0.1:8765
How It Works

1. Get a Task Queue — Drafted or Hand-Written

Describe the work in plain words and the wizard drafts tasks.yaml for you — or write it yourself, or import it from a SPEC.md. Either way a human confirms the draft before anything runs.

  • Wizard: repo scan + baseline + clarifying questions + cost forecast
  • Recipes render deterministically — no LLM call, $0
  • Lint catches contract errors and fragile acceptance before launch
  • Edit the draft as task cards in the browser UI
tasks.yaml
tasks:
  - id: port-validator
    scope_paths: ["tools-ts/**"]
    acceptance:
      - "cd tools-ts && npm test"
    budget:
      max_cost_usd: 0.50
    gate: milestone-1

2. Agent Loop with Guardrails

The coder agent gets read_file, write_file, list_dir, and run_command — nothing else.

  • Writes locked to task scope paths
  • canon/ always read-only
  • npm install blocked at tool level
  • Violations logged as events
$ forge run --tasks tasks.yaml --target ./my-repo
[run] started 2026-08-20T10:00:00Z
[coder] port-validator → DONE (12 steps)
[validate] npm test → exit=0
[review] APPROVE
[git] committed to forge/port-validator
[done] port-validator — $0.17

3. Human Gate Before Merge

Nothing merges automatically. When a gated task reaches done, the run pauses until you explicitly accept it. A task stuck on a budget cap or a dispute can also be accepted as an explicit owner override.

  • forge accept <task-id> merges branch — or overrides blocked/failed
  • forge resume continues queue
  • Runs resumable from disk snapshots, kill the process any time
  • Full journal in runs/<id>/events.jsonl
bash
# Gate #3 — human approval
$ forge accept port-validator
Merged forge/port-validator into main.

$ forge resume run-20260820-080204
Continuing 3 remaining tasks...
Command Reference
forge init [--target DIR] [--profile careful|normal|fast]Prepare a project: stack detection, git init, skeleton tasks.yaml, baseline checks
forge wizard --prompt "..." [--recipe NAME] [--yes]Draft tasks, acceptance, budgets and gates from plain words or a recipe; asks clarifying questions; prints a cost forecast
forge import --spec SPEC.md [--out FILE]Draft a task queue from an existing specification via the planner
forge lint tasks.yamlPre-flight validation: contract errors + frozen-acceptance advice
forge run --tasks F [--target DIR] [--spec S] [--dry-run]Run the queue; --dry-run prints a cost forecast and executes nothing
forge resume <run_id>Continue a stopped or paused run from on-disk history snapshots
forge status [run_id]Task table: state, tokens, cost, repairs, notes
forge log <task-id>Full event journal of one task
forge report [run_id] [--plain]Cost/token summary; --plain — human-readable outcome and next steps
forge accept <task-id>Human gate #3: accept a done task (merge branch); manual override for blocked/failed
forge ui [--port 8765]Read-only web dashboard: kanban, log viewer, cost report, wizard-draft editor at /wizard?file=…
Use Cases

Language Ports

Port a Python validator to TypeScript, a Bash script to Go, or a legacy module to a new framework — with acceptance tests ensuring parity.

Spec-Driven Modules

Turn a SPEC.md into a working feature: the planner drafts tasks, the coder implements, and tests prove correctness.

Refactoring at Scale

Update 20 files to a new API, rename symbols across packages, or migrate test suites — one task per module.

Test Generation

Generate missing unit tests for legacy code. Acceptance commands run new tests against old code.

Documentation Sync

Keep READMEs, API docs, and decision records in sync with code changes.

Multi-Repo Updates

Run the same task queue against multiple repositories. Each gets its own branch, journal, and cost tracking.

Quick Start
bash
# 1. Install from GitHub (Python ≥ 3.12)
git clone https://github.com/Xarawg/agent-forge.git
cd agent-forge
python -m venv .venv && source .venv/Scripts/activate  # .venv/bin/activate on Linux/macOS
pip install -e .

# 2. Verify in mock mode — no API key needed
FORGE_MOCK=1 pytest -q
FORGE_MOCK=1 forge run --tasks config/tasks.example.yaml --target /tmp/demo
forge status && forge report --plain

# 3. Point it at your project (any state: empty, legacy, documented)
forge init --target /path/to/project
forge wizard --target /path/to/project --prompt "what you want, in plain words"
# review the draft → tasks.wizard.yaml (gate #1 is you)

# 4. Real run — add a provider key to .env first (DeepSeek, OpenRouter, Ollama)
forge run --tasks /path/to/project/tasks.wizard.yaml --target /path/to/project
forge accept <task-id>   # human gate, then
forge resume <run_id>
forge report --plain       # plain-language outcome
forge ui                   # kanban on http://127.0.0.1:8765
Why agent-forge?

Budget Caps

Per-task, per-run, and per-day USD limits. Exceed a cap and the task becomes blocked with a reason — no runaway bills.

Scope Control

File writes are locked to the paths you allow; canon/ writes and dependency installs are blocked in code. Command execution uses a tests/linters allowlist — a guardrail, not a sandbox (trust model).

Second Model Review

A cheaper reviewer model checks every result against a checklist. Failures enter a bounded repair loop (≤3 iterations).

Full Audit Trail

Every token, every command, every cost is written to runs/<id>/events.jsonl.

Mock Mode

Test the entire pipeline without an API key. Perfect for CI and local development.

Any Provider

DeepSeek, OpenRouter free tiers, local Ollama, or your own endpoint. Presets are YAML — no code changes.

Honest Stops

DISPUTE / STUCK / BLOCKED markers halt a task visibly when spec and reality disagree — a human resolves contradictions, never the model.

Resumable Runs

Dialogue history is snapshotted after every agent step. Kill the process, reboot, come back tomorrow — forge resume picks up mid-task with context intact.

Plain-Language Reports

forge report --plain answers three questions — what got done, what failed, what to do next — without reading a single YAML file.
